title: Size at female morphometric maturity in Pachygrapsus crassipes Randall, 1840 (Decapoda: Brachyura: Grapsidae): sexual size dimorphisms of pleons and chelipeds, with notes on morphological associations with parasitic rhizocephalan infections
content:
Abstract
Sexual maturation in brachyuran crabs is often accompanied by sex-specific allometric changes in the pleon and chelipeds. Rhizocephalan infection, however, can feminize male secondary sexual characters. We examined these relationships in 280 individuals of Pachygrapsus crassipes Randall, 1840 collected from the Boso Peninsula, Japan. Carapace width (CW), pleon width (PW), and cheliped propodus length (PrL) and width (PrW) were measured. Gaussian-mixture and related classifications identified 10 externally negative males with unusually broad pleons as suspected infections and separated externally negative females into eight immature and 71 mature individuals, including 15 ovigerous females. A bias-reduced binomial model estimated female median size at morphometric maturity as 10.55 mm CW (95% CI 8.81–11.66 mm); this interval was conditional on the final morphometric classifications. Female PW increased more steeply with CW than male PW, whereas male chela dimensions increased more steeply than those of females. Male-biased dimorphism became statistically detectable at approximately 11.7 mm CW for PrL and at 12.1–13.0 mm CW for PrW. In the primary analysis, the Bayesian information criterion weakly supported a male PrW breakpoint at 22.00 mm CW (95% CI 18.27–26.47 mm), whereas no PrL breakpoint was supported. Male morphometric maturity therefore could not be estimated robustly from cheliped allometry. Males with external signs of infection had broader pleons and shallower chela growth trajectories than externally negative males. After CW was controlled, greater proportional PW enlargement within infection-positive males was associated with larger proportional reductions in both PrL and PrW. These findings establish a population-specific allometric baseline for female morphometric maturity and sexual size dimorphism and are consistent with rhizocephalan-associated morphological feminization of male pleons and chelipeds.
